title: Fractions
sub: Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions

steps.html:
Fractions

14 = 28: same amount, cut into more pieces. Multiply top and bottom by the same number.
say: Today: fractions. The bottom number says how many equal pieces. The top says how many you have.
One fourth is the same amount as two eighths. Just cut into more pieces. Multiplying the top and bottom by the same number never changes the value.

steps.html:
Adding: make the bottoms match

23 + 14
common bottom: 12 → 812 + 312
= 1112

Add the tops only. The bottom stays 12.
say: To add or subtract, the bottoms must match.
Two thirds plus one fourth. Both three and four go into twelve. Two thirds is eight twelfths, one fourth is three twelfths.
Never add the bottoms. The size of the pieces doesn't change.

steps.okSay: Yes! Fourteen twenty-firsts minus six twenty-firsts is eight twenty-firsts.
steps.noSay: Not quite. Use twenty-one as the bottom. Two thirds is fourteen twenty-firsts and two sevenths is six twenty-firsts. The difference is eight twenty-firsts.

steps.html:
Multiplying: straight across

15 × 512 = 560 = 112
Shortcut: cancel first: the 5s cancel → 112
say: Multiplying is the easy one. No common bottom needed.
Top times top, bottom times bottom. One fifth times five twelfths is five sixtieths, which simplifies to one twelfth.
Even faster: cancel before you multiply. The fives cancel, leaving one twelfth.

steps.html:
Dividing: keep, change, flip

34 ÷ 35
keep 34, change ÷ to ×, flip 35 → 53
34 × 53 = 1512 = 54
say: Dividing fractions uses a famous rule: keep, change, flip.
Keep the first fraction, change divide to multiply, and flip the second fraction upside down.
Three fourths times five thirds is fifteen twelfths, which simplifies to five fourths.

steps.okSay: Yes! Two thirds is about zero point six seven, the biggest.
steps.no: Turn them into decimals: 0.6, 0.625, 0.583, 0.667. 23 is the greatest.
steps.noSay: Not quite. As decimals they're about zero point six, zero point six two five, zero point five eight, and zero point six seven. Two thirds is the biggest.

say: Great! Now 4 practice questions. You'll see the answer and an explanation after each one.
Last part: three checkpoint questions. Get two out of three to finish the lesson. You've got this!

steps.html:
Remember

1. Same value: multiply top and bottom by the same number.

2. + −: common bottom, then add the tops only.

3. ×: straight across (cancel first). ÷: keep, change, flip.
say: Let's review. Multiply the top and bottom by the same number to make equal fractions.
To add or subtract, get a common bottom and add only the tops.
Multiply straight across, and to divide, keep, change, flip. Great job!
